issues.description: The problem statement (UML and text) specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void on SealSaloon and instructs students to call checkOrderReady() from orderMeal(). However, the solution implements checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) and orderMeal invokes checkOrderReady(true). This is a signature mismatch between the specification and the reference solution. Students following the specification will implement a no-arg method and will find the reference solution uses a different signature (and extra debug behavior), which can be confusing and may hide intended usage or test expectations.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the reference solution match the specified signature: implement a no-argument public void checkOrderReady() (and remove the boolean parameter). If logging is desired internally, use an internal flag or a separate private logging mechanism, or provide an overloaded no-arg method that calls the parameterized one with a default value. Alternatively, update the problem statement to explicitly document the boolean parameter and its purpose so the API contract is clear.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void (used by orderMeal and described as the routine that serves ready orders). The solution implementation defines checkOrderReady with a boolean parameter (checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)). Although the method name is the same, the added parameter changes the expected API and can confuse students: the problem spec and class diagram indicate a zero-argument method that students should implement or call, while the solution requires an extra argument (breaking a straightforward mapping between the spec and implementation).
issues.suggested_fix: Align the method signature with the problem specification: provide a public void checkOrderReady() no-argument method. If internal logging is desired, implement an internal/private overload (e.g., private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging)) and have the public checkOrderReady() call it with a default value. This preserves the API students expect while keeping any extra logging behavior internal.
